evidence: app/package.json:11-16 — vite ^8.3.5 (current npm latest, published 2026-10-21) and typescript ^7.0.2 (current stable, 2026-07-08), zero runtime deps
app/tsconfig.json:2-10 — target ES2023, moduleResolution 'bundler', isolatedModules, types ['vite/client'] — the current recommended TS/Vite pairing

app/src/api.ts:9-13 — import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL, still the documented Vite 8 env API (vite.dev/guide/env-and-mode), with a runtime-injected global preferred so the API origin can change without rebuilding
absence of a vite.config — zero-config app with no legacy options (e.g. no optimizeDeps.esbuildOptions, no Rollup-only plugins)
latest_apis.rationale: On both current majors within months of their release (Vite 8/Rolldown in March 2026, TS 7 native in July 2026), no compat shims, no config the next release would generate differently. Sources: vite.dev/blog/announcing-vite8 and devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:94-102 — fetch with a per-URL in-flight Promise cache; failures evicted, no hand-rolled XHR or library
app/src/main.ts:25,61 / app/src/pages/home.ts:34-52 — URL and URLSearchParams for all routing/filter state; format.ts:35 findLast (ES2023); move.ts:14 replaceAll
app/src/dom.ts:35-38 — native Element.replaceChildren and appendChild (no innerHTML string building, which also removes an XSS class)
app/server.mjs:54 — AbortSignal.timeout(3000) on the API probe; server.mjs:74 res.body?.cancel() (modern undidi/streams idioms); node:fs/promises, path, url/fileURLToPath
app/src/components.ts:64-69 — native img lazy loading/decoding/async with width/height to prevent CLS; app/src/pages/home.ts:120-127 native form controls with labels
app/src/style.css — CSS custom properties, grid, aspect-ratio, :focus-visible, columns/break-inside, image-rendering: pixelated; no polyfills or preprocessor
platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform everywhere; the only hand-rolled pieces (h() helper, sortable table) are conveniences over the DOM, not polyfills. The single gap is that page fetches aren't passed an AbortSignal, so stale navigations complete in the background (app/src/api.ts:94).

evidence: app/package.json:5-17 — devDependencies only: typescript and vite, both at current stable majors; no runtime dependencies at all
app/server.mjs:6-10 — production server is ~120 lines of node:http + node:fs, avoiding express or any server framework
app/src/dom.ts / app/src/table.ts — DOM construction, list rendering and sortable tables all hand-built in ~150 lines rather than pulling lit/preact/jQuery
dependencies.rationale: Two devDependencies, both current and minimal; everything else the app needs (router, server, table sorting, caching) is small first-party code over web/Node platform APIs. Nothing to prune, nothing outdated.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:20-110 — all API shapes behind one module with explicit interfaces (Species, Pokemon, Move, Ability, Type, Generation) and typed accessors; pages never fetch directly except via get()/getResource()

app/src/url-state.ts:1-17 — URL/history mutation centralized; app/src/format.ts — all naming/display rules in one place; app/src/components.ts:44 — single section() helper guarantees the region/aria-labelledby pattern app-wide
app/src/main.ts:44-47 — error handling typed via NotFoundError boundary instead of string checks
app/server.mjs:40-47 vs app/src/main.ts:20-27 — route regexes duplicated between server and client; adding/removing a route touches both and they can drift silently
app/src/pages/home.ts:57-58 — idFromUrl logic re-implemented inline instead of importing format.ts:25's helper

app/src/pages/home.ts:127-133 — 150ms debounce timer survives navigation: typing then immediately clicking a card lets the timer fire on the detached page and history.replaceState the Pokémon URL back to a filtered home URL (app/src/url-state.ts:12); main.ts's navigation token isn't shared with pages, so async page work guards itself inconsistently (pokemon.ts has its own token, home.ts has none)
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, URL state, formatting and landmark markup each live behind one well-typed module, so an API or spec change is mostly localized; knocked down one notch by the duplicated route tables between server.mjs and main.ts, the inline idFromUrl copy, and page-level async work (debounce, in-flight renders) with no shared cancellation/unmount convention.

findings.issue: The search debounce timer isn't cancelled when the page is replaced; firing after navigation to another route calls updateUrl, which history.replaceState's the new page's URL with a filtered home URL, corrupting the back/forward history.
findings.suggestion: Give Page an unmounted/disposal hook invoked from main.ts's render(), or pass the shared navigation token into pages so async callbacks can bail (as pokemon.ts's moveSection already does with its own token).

findings.issue: RESOURCE_ROUTES duplicates the route patterns from app/src/main.ts:20; the two tables will drift the first time a route is added or renamed, and there's no cross-reference comment.
findings.suggestion: Derive both from one source of truth (e.g. a small JSON/route manifest emitted to dist at build time, or have main.ts export its patterns and generate a JS fragment the server can import), or at minimum add a TODO linking each to the other.

findings.issue: ID-from-URL parsing is re-implemented inline (Number(url.match(...))) when format.ts:25 already exports idFromUrl, used everywhere else.
get() fetches aren't given an AbortSignal; navigating away lets stale requests run to completion (rendered correctly guarded by tokens, but bandwidth/timing waste).
findings.suggestion: Accept an optional signal in get() and wire it to per-navigation aborts from main.ts.

findings.issue: history.scrollRestoration = 'auto' sets the default explicitly; a no-op that invites the misreading that the app manages scroll manually.
findings.suggestion: Delete the line, or set it to 'manual' if custom scroll handling is intended.

findings.issue: document.getElementById('main')! — the index.html contract is enforced only by a non-null assertion; if #main disappears the app blanks with a cryptic TypeError.
findings.suggestion: Guard with an explicit throw (or console.error + a visible message) so the failure names the missing element.

findings.issue: isolatedModules is on but verbatimModuleSyntax isn't, so import type discipline relies on convention (mostly followed, e.g. app/src/main.ts:4) rather than the compiler; noUncheckedIndexedAccess is also absent.
findings.suggestion: Add verbatimModuleSyntax: true (and consider noUncheckedIndexedAccess) — TS's current recommendation for ESM/bundler projects.

summary: This is the lean, current-generation vanilla TS + Vite app you'd want as a template: Vite 8 (Rolldown) and TypeScript 7 at their latest stable releases, zero runtime dependencies, a first-party ~120-line node:http server, and platform-first code (fetch/URL/URLSearchParams/replaceChildren/lazy images, custom-property CSS) with no polyfills or legacy API usage. All data access, URL state, formatting and landmark markup sit behind single well-typed modules, so API or spec movement is mostly localized. The deductions are modest: duplicated route tables between server.mjs and main.ts, an uncancelled debounce timer that can rewrite history after navigation, and one inline re-implementation of idFromUrl — cheap fixes that would make it fully exemplary.
